title: WPSB/235/2015 of Himanshu Verma Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
 *******************
 Writ Petition No. 235 of 2015 (S/B)
Himanshu Verma ..............Petitioner
Versus
State of Uttarakhand and others ...........Respondents
Mr. B.D.Upadhyaya, Senior Advocate, assisted by Mr. Sunil Upadhyaya,
Advocate, present for the writ petitioner.
Mr. S.S.Chauhan, learned Deputy Advocate General, present for the
State/respondents no. 1 & 2.
Mr. D.S.Patni, Advocate, present for the respondent no. 3.
Mr. Rakesh Thapalyal, Advocate, present for the respondent no.4.
.Coram : Hon'ble K.M.Joseph, C. J.
 Hon'ble U.C. Dhyani, J.
K.M.Joseph, C. J. (oral)

Prayers in the writ petition are as follows:
A. Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of
mandamus commanding the respondents not to make
promotions in either of the department (Uttarakhand Pey
Jal Nigam and Uttarakhand Jal Sansthan) until the
process of unification/provincialization is in progress.
B. Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of
mandamus commanding the respondents not to declare
the result in case any DPC has been convened.
C. Issue any other writ, order or direction which this
Hon'ble Court may deem fit and proper in the nature and
circumstances of the case.
 Briefly put, the case of the petitioner is as follows:

2
 Petitioner is a regular employee of the Uttarakhand
Pay Jal Nigam. He seeks to interdict the promotion to be
carried out by the 4th respondent. This is on the supposition
that the proposal for unification and provincialisation of the
two bodies, namely, the 3rd and 4th respondents, which are
under consideration, is fructified. The result being, accordingly
to the petitioner, the juniors of the petitioner in the 4th
respondent will be enable to steal a march over him. There is
also a reference to the position of the 4th respondent on giving
relaxation to "junior of the petitioner" in the 4th respondent
enabling him to steal a march over which will affect his right,
runs the argument.
 We heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and
the learned counsel appearing on behalf of the respondents,
namely, respondents no. 3 & 4.
 As of now, we are unable to perceive, how the
petitioner can claim to be senior to somebody else, who is
working in a different corporation as unification has not yet
taken place. No doubt the petitioner has a case that
Government itself decided to put matters on hold. It is a matter
entirely for the 4th respondent, no doubt subject to the lawful
orders by the Government, which may be passed, to take a
decision as to what is the policy to be adopted. Petitioner has
not made out any case for interference by the Court for a writ
of mandamus, which he is seeking.
 Accordingly, the writ petition fails and is dismissed.
 No order as to costs.
